content:
alisa (Customer Success): FYI customer ACME-57 reporting a jump in 5xx on the streaming endpoint since ~09:10 UTC. Around 15-20% of streams are getting 502/504 mid-session, and they're seeing double billing for retried chunks. They have a handful of request IDs: rQk1v2, rQk1v3, rQk1v7.
maria (Support): Thanks — opening thread. Can you paste one full request id + response headers/partial body? Also, are they using our JS SDK or direct HTTP?
alisa (Customer Success): They're on our JS SDK v2.3.1, streaming generate + keepalive disabled on client. Example curl we asked them to run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large", "stream":true, "prompt":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```
kevin (Eng): Noted. Are these failing mid-stream (after a few chunks) or failing to establish?
alisa (Customer Success): Mostly mid-stream after 3-8 chunks. Client shows keepalive then a short pause then connection reset/502.
devon (SRE): Correlating with infra metrics now. Early signal: edge LB connection_pool_saturation spiked for tenant acme-org between 09:08-09:18. Backend 502_rate jumped from 0.5% -> 18%. Query I ran: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/edge?tenant=acme-org | jq .` — shows kvcache_lock_waits increasing.
sam (SDK): Quick thought — v2.3.1 introduced prefetch + aggressive kvcache warm-up on stream start. If prefetch holds a kvcache lock while client sends chunks it can amplify contention under many concurrent streams. We saw a similar pattern in internal loadtest but only for keepalive-disabled clients. You can disable prefetch in the SDK runtime: `client.options.prefetch = false` (temporary).
kevin (Eng): Good call. Can we reproduce locally with a small script? Here's a quick loop I used to mimic the customer's pattern (200 concurrent streams, short chunk intervals):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  node stream_client.js --no-keepalive &
done
```
stream_client.js simulates sending 3 small chunks then waits. This drives kvcache work and reveals lock contention.
devon (SRE): Confirmed: ran a scaled repro in staging and hit the same 502 spike when prefetch enabled + keepalive disabled. Logs show repeated `kvcache: lock_wait > 200ms` and downstream gateway returning 502 on connection reset.
maria (Support): Immediate mitigation options?
devon (SRE): Two quick mitigations we can do: 1) apply per-tenant connection cap for acme-org in the edge router (throttle new streams) and 2) route them to a lower-concurrency pool (dedicated smaller model variant) to reduce simultaneous kvcache pressure. I can flip the cap now.
maria (Support): Please do, and I'll tell the customer we've throttled new streams and are working on an SDK patch.
devon (SRE): Cap applied at 09:34 UTC: new_streams_rate limit = 100/min for acme-org. Observed backend 502_rate fall from ~18% -> 0.8% within 2 minutes. p95 stream latency improved from 1.9s -> 420ms.
sam (SDK): We'll push a patch to v2.3.x that disables prefetch by default for streaming clients and add a config flag. ETA for patch and staged rollout: 6 hours. Recommend customer upgrade after we release.
maria (Support): Noted — I'll update the customer: temporary throttling put in place, engineering reproduced root cause (kvcache lock contention + prefetch), SDK patch coming, and long-term: we'll add server-side per-stream backpressure and improve kvcache lock granularity.
sre-bot: alert resolved for acme-org (502 spike) — duration 0h26m, tickets linked: #SUP-1192.
alisa (Customer Success): Customer acknowledged the temporary mitigation and asked for ETA on SDK patch. I'll keep the customer on weekly sync until patch rollout. Thanks team :thumbsup:
